classification.difficultyReason: Select equal-chord, equal-radius, diameter and full-turn relations, then link a few familiar angle calculations across six given figures; no unprompted theorem proof.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, giving reasons.

spec.description: Circle with centre O and points U, T, S, R in order around its upper arc. Chords UT, TS and SR have matching double ticks. Radii OU, OT, OS and OR are drawn. ∠SOR = 50°, ∠TOS = θ and ∠TUO = α.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: The three equal chords subtend equal central angles, so $\theta=\angle UOT=50^\circ$. Triangle UOT is isosceles, so $\alpha=\frac{(180^\circ-50^\circ)}{2}=65^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O and points A, B, C across the upper-left and upper circumference. AO, AB and BC have matching double ticks. OB and OC are drawn. α marks ∠AOB. β marks the reflex angle AOC, passing below and to the right of O.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: OA=OB are radii and OA=AB is marked, so AOB is equilateral and $\alpha=60^\circ$. Also BC=AB=radius, so BOC is equilateral. The indicated reflex angle is $\beta=360^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=240^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O. R, O and P are collinear, forming diameter RP. Q lies on the upper-left circumference. QP, QR and QO are drawn. Matching double ticks mark QR = RO. θ marks ∠QPR.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: RQ=RO is given and OQ=OR are radii, so RQO is equilateral and $\angle QRO=60^\circ$. As RP is a diameter, $\angle RQP=90^\circ$. In triangle RQP, $\theta=180^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC inscribed in a circle with centre O; B is above O, A lower-left and C lower-right. OA, OB and OC are drawn. ∠AOC has a right-angle marker and ∠BOC = 130°. α marks ∠OAC, β marks ∠OBC and γ marks ∠ABO.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: OA=OC and $\angle AOC=90^\circ$, so $\alpha=45^\circ$. OB=OC and $\angle BOC=130^\circ$, so $\beta=\frac{(180^\circ-130^\circ)}{2}=25^\circ$. Around O, $\angle AOB=360^\circ-90^\circ-130^\circ=140^\circ$. Since OA=OB, $\gamma=\frac{(180^\circ-140^\circ)}{2}=20^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O. G, O and F lie on a diameter, with G above and F below. H lies on the upper-left circumference. HG, HF and HO are drawn. A leader labelled 25° points to ∠OHF. θ marks ∠HOG.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: OH=OF, so triangle HOF has equal base angles of $25^\circ$. Hence $\angle HOF=180^\circ-2(25^\circ)=130^\circ$. Since F,O,G are collinear, $\theta=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with centre O divided by radii to ten circumference vertices. The ten consecutive chords have matching double ticks. On the right, C, B and A label consecutive vertices from upper-right downward. α marks ∠BOA and β marks ∠OBA.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: The ten equal chords subtend ten equal central angles, so $\alpha=\frac{360^\circ}{10}=36^\circ$. In isosceles triangle AOB, $\beta=\frac{(180^\circ-36^\circ)}{2}=72^\circ$.
